texts.preamble: The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep on 5 February, 2026 Author: Gurpal Singh Ahluwalia Bench: G. S. Ahluwalia Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:5944 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice G. S. Ahluwalia On The 5 th Of February, 2026 Miscellaneous Second Appeal No. 10 of 2025 State Of Madhya Pradesh Versus Pradeep And Others Appearance: Shri S.S. Kushwah - Government Advocate for appellant/Stat Shri Sanjay Bahirani and Shri Harshad Bahirani - Advocates Order
texts.facts: 1. This Miscellaneous Second Appeal under Section 71 (6) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 has been filed against the order dated 28.05.2024 passed by Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/Second District Judge, District Morena in MCA No.67/2022, by which the appeal filed by respondents was allowed and the order dated 24.02.2022 passed by the Adjudicating Authority/Additional District Magistrate Morena in case No.01/2020/Food Safety, was [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 2. According to the prosecution case, on 26/07/2019, the house of respondent No.1 was searched by the Food Safety Officer in presence of respondent No.1. It was found that 153 sealed tins of Kamani crisp refined palm kernel oil were stored. On inquiry, respondent No.1 informed that the basement of his house was given by him to respondent No.2 on rent, who is in the business of dairy. Respondent No.1 could not produce the rent note, bills of purchase of the palm oil. The samples of the palm oil were collected. NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 2 MSA-10-2025 The Food Analyst found that they were an adulterant under Section 3(1)(a) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. An FIR, bearing crime No.478/2019, was also registered at the Police Station Kailaras District Morena for offences under Sections 420, 272, 273, 120-B of IPC and Sections 51 and 59 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, against respondents. A copy of the report of the Food Analyst was served on the respondents and both of them gave it in writing that they do not want to get the samples re-tested from the Referral Laboratory. In reply to the show cause notice, respondent No.1 had also The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62493681/ 1 provided a copy of rent note to show that the basement was given on rent to respondent No. 2 on 10.06.2019 for a period of 11 months. The Adjudicating Authority, after recording evidence, held that the appellants were guilty of violating the provisions of Section 26(2) and their act is punishable under Sections 57(1) and 58 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, and accordingly, imposed a fine of Rs.2,00,000/- each on respondents No.1 and 2 under Section 57 of the FSSA, and a fine of Rs. 2,00,000/- each on them under Section 58 of the FSSA, i.e. total Rs.4 Lac each was imposed on the respondents No.1 & 2. 3. Being aggrieved by the said order, respondents No.1 and 2 preferred an appeal which was registered as MCA No.67/2022 and, by order dated 28/05/2024, the Food Safety Appellate Tribunal/Second District Judge Morena [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order passed by the Adjudicating Authority primarily on the ground that the seized palm oil was not examined within a period of 14 days and the Food Analyst had started the testing after 103 days of collection of samples and there is nothing on record to suggest that the Food NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 3 MSA-10-2025 Analyst had informed the competent authority with regard to delay in carrying out the test as required under Section 46(3) of the Food Safety and Standards Act and Food Safety Officer did not visit the dairy of respondent No.2 and did not collect any sample from there. The entire action was taken by Food Safety Officer merely on suspicion that respondent No.2 must be using the palm oil for the purposes of adulterating milk. Merely because the Food Analyst had declared the palm oil as an adulterant, it cannot be said that respondent No.2 had stored the aforesaid palm oil with an intention to mix it with milk. So far as respondent No.1 is concerned, it was held that though the place from where it was recovered was in his possession of respondent No.1, but there is nothing on record to suggest that respondent No.1 was jointly running the business of dairy along with respondent No.2. 4. This Court on 03.02.2026 had passed the following order : "It is submitted by counsel for appellant that 153 sealed tins of palm oil were seized from the basement of the house of respondent No.1, and it was the case of respondent No.1 that the said articles were owned by respondent No.2, who is having his milk dairy in Jaura. It is submitted by counsel for appellant that the appellate tribunal has [LEAKAGE_MASK] the order passed by the adjudicating authority on the ground that the prosecution has failed to prove that the respondent No.2 was having any dairy in Jaura and no samples were collected from the dairy and the respondent No.1 cannot be punished only for giving the premises on rent to respondent No.2. In the considered opinion of this Court, the appellate tribunal has lost certain important aspects which are required to be adjudicated. (i.) Whether the respondent No.1 had any building permission to construct a basement in his house ? The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Pradeep on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62493681/ 2 (ii.) If there was any building permission, then whether the said basement could have been let out to the respondent No.2 for storage of huge quantity of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 4 MSA-10-2025 palm oil ? (iii.) Whether the respondent No.2 was having any dairy in Jaura, as it is submitted by Shri Bahirani that the respondent number No.2 was not having any dairy in Jaura. Accordingly, respondent No.1 is directed to file the building permission of the house from where the 153 sealed tins of palm oil were recovered. If the building permission contains the permission to construct a basement, then the respondent No.1 shall also clarify that for what purposes the basement could have been constructed, and whether it could have been used for commercial purposes or not ? Counsel for respondent No.2 is also directed to make a categorical statement as to whether the respondent No.2 is running any milk dairy in Tehsil Jaura, District Morena, or not, and if not, then whether he is giving his no objection to the action which the local administration can take against the said dairy by sealing the same. As prayed, list on 05.02.2026 ." 5. In response to the aforesaid order, the respondents have filed a copy of the building permission to show that the Gram Panchayat Antri Janpad Panchayat Kailaras District Morena had granted No Objection Certificate for building construction on 18/02/2015 and the layout plan for the basement, showroom, first floor and second floor was passed by Gram Panchayat Antri. 6. Similarly, counsel for State has provided a copy of a licence dated 13.06.2024 issued in favour of respondent No.2 for manufacturing and trading of dairy and milk products.
texts.arguments: 8. However, it is submitted by counsel for appellant that the appellate Tribunal should have remanded the matter back to the Adjudicating NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5944 5 MSA-10-2025 Authority because respondent No.2 in his evidence has stated the he does not own any dairy but he only sells packed tins of palm oil. It is submitted that respondent No.2 has not produced any document to show that he had any business of selling palm oil only. It is further submitted that appellate Tribunal lost sight of fact that generally basements are to be used for parking purposes and not for any other purposes and under what circumstances, the respondent No.1 stored large quantity of palm oil has also not been explained by him. On the contrary, he had merely stated that he had let out the basement to respondent No.2 and that the palm oil was of respondent No.2.

It is submitted that respondent No.2 has not produced any document to show that he had any business of selling palm oil only. It is further submitted that appellate Tribunal lost sight of fact that generally basements are to be used for parking purposes and not for any other purposes and under what circumstances, the respondent No.1 stored large quantity of palm oil has also not been explained by him. On the contrary, he had merely stated that he had let out the basement to respondent No.2 and that the palm oil was of respondent No.2.
